name: GPT Infraprojects Ltd
title: GPT Infraprojects Ltd - 533761 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GPT Infra Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 5% to INR291 crores and EBITDA margin hit 14.2%; management now guides FY27 revenue of INR1,600 crores plus.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue grew about 2% YoY to INR275 crores, while consolidated revenue rose about 5% to INR291 crores, so H1 consolidated revenue was nearly flat at INR594 crores. Margins improved: standalone EBITDA rose 17.7% to INR44 crores at 16% margin, and consolidated EBITDA was INR41 crores at 14.2%. Management blamed West Bengal elections and an extended monsoon for H1 execution moderation, and said billing and workforce availability recovered in October. Full-year guidance was trimmed to 25-27% growth from the earlier 27-30%, and the company needs about INR1,000 crores of H2 revenue.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR262 crores (about 90% of total) and EBIT INR33 crores (about 92% of EBIT); order book INR4,521 crores. Growth came from Prayagraj Ganga Bridge, Kolaghat and Kona Expressway.

segments.name: Concrete Sleepers
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR30 crores (about 10%) and EBIT INR2.5 crores; order book a record INR852 crores (about 16% of total), supported by domestic and export supplies including Africa.

segments.name: Alcon (railway signaling subsidiary)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue about INR36 crores with EBITDA close to 20%. Order book about INR480 crores, its highest ever. FY27 revenue target INR150 crores; FY28 INR200 crores plus.

segments.name: Africa operations
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue expected about INR80 crores, mainly South Africa and Ghana. Subsidiary won a 5-year INR385 crore Transnet Freight Rail contract, expected to add about INR70-75 crores a year in South Africa.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR1,600 crores, implying about INR1,000 crores in H2 (about INR160 crores per month).
Full-year growth now guided at 25-27%, down from the earlier 27-30% range.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 14-15%, supported by signaling and Africa.
FY27 order inflow target minimum INR3,000 crores; about INR1,490 crores secured so far, with at least INR2,000 crores expected in H2.
Alcon FY27 revenue about INR150 crores and EBITDA about INR30 crores; domestic sleeper business expected to grow about 15% over the next two years.
Management expects to convert the order book into execution over the next 2 to 2.5 years.
capex_capacity: Order book about INR5,373 crores, about 4.3 times FY26 revenue; up from INR4,303 crores in Q1 FY27.
Q2 order wins: INR484 crores RVNL EPC bridge over Mahanadi (544 m open web girder), Alcon signaling contracts about INR428 crores, and INR385 crore Transnet 5-year contract.
Alcon can bid for individual contracts up to INR200 crores plus in its own name; this is expected to rise after the proposed merger with the parent.
Working capital cycle being reduced; management says the current balance sheet can support growth.
Contract assets about INR543 crores; about INR10 crores is over one year old and the rest is current. Retention money held by clients is about INR100 crores.
demand_pricing: Management says recovery started in October with significant billing; realisations from old receivables also helped cash flow.
Domestic sleeper business expected to grow about 15% over two years, including inflation and volume growth.
Management said most contracts have price escalation protection; currency and political risk are the main international concerns.
Railway signaling market opportunity cited at about USD 1.5 billion, with planned railway outlay of about USD 1 trillion over six years.
No project in which GPT is currently L1; company says it will disclose L1 positions to exchanges.
Two new West Bengal bridge connectivity contracts worth about INR2,100 crores announced in the state budget; company expects to win one or two.

qa_highlights.question: How can the company reach its FY27 growth target given H1 performance and the need for about INR1,100 crores in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of INR1,000 plus crores in H2, taking full-year growth to 25-27% against the earlier 27-30% range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract assets rise about INR55 crores since March, and how much is over a year old?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract assets rose about INR45 crores in six months due to new projects (Chambal, Kashi Ganga Bridge, Rapti) not yet billed. About INR10 crores of the INR543 crores is over one year old.

qa_highlights.question: What were Alcon's H1 revenue and EBITDA, and what is its FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 revenue was about INR36 crores with EBITDA close to 20%. FY27 revenue is expected at about INR150 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book increase is from recent wins, and what is the inflow status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR1,400 crores of wins in the year drove the increase, with about INR1,450 crores secured so far against the INR3,000 crore target.

qa_highlights.question: When will revenue growth accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 growth of about 40% on recovered execution, after the monsoon and elections affected Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any L1 position in the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is currently no project where GPT is L1; it will announce any L1 position to the exchanges.

qa_highlights.question: Do contract assets convert to P&L revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract assets include retention, unbilled revenue and price escalation. The H1 increase was about INR15-20 crores for the contract-asset build (unbilled revenue).

risks_watch: H2 revenue of about INR1,000 crores is a large step-up from H1 (about INR594 crores consolidated), and it depends on the monsoon ending and workforce recovery.
Full-year guidance was trimmed from 27-30% to 25-27%.
Contract assets of about INR543 crores and retention of about INR100 crores; billing on Chambal and other new projects must come through.
Alcon goodwill amortisation of INR8 crores in H1 weighs on reported PAT until the merger.
Africa exposure carries currency and political risks; the Transnet contract is still early in execution.
No L1 positions currently disclosed, so order inflow target of INR3,000 crores depends on converting pending bids.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H2 and order inflows, with specific numbers, but cautious on H1, which management attributes to temporary factors. Management trimmed the full-year growth range and was vague on the timing of revenue acceleration and the margin target.
key_quotes: With workforce availability now normalized, execution is gaining momentum.

We are very confident that the EBITDA margins will be in the range of 14% to 15% on a consolidated basis, and this is due to the addition of the high -margin signaling business and the Africa operations picking up quite well.
Currently there is no project in which we are L1, and we will come back to the stock exchanges once we are L1.

growth.why: FY27 growth guidance cut to 25-27% from 27-30%, implying about INR1,000 crores H2 revenue, backed by a INR5,373 crore order book and Alcon/Africa targets, but H1 consolidated revenue was nearly flat and no new capacity was quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin rose to 16% in Q2 (+215 bps YoY) and consolidated margin is guided at 14-15% for FY27, supported by Alcon (about 20% EBITDA margin) and Africa mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning was quantified in the call; growth is framed around order book execution over 2-2.5 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H2 consolidated revenue of about INR1,000 crores is needed versus INR594 crores in H1 (about 68% step-up), backed by a INR5,373 crore order book (about 4.3x FY26 revenue), though management trimmed FY27 growth to 25-27%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; management says the current balance sheet can support growth and working capital is being reduced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth guidance was cut to 25-27% from 27-30%, and H1 consolidated revenue was nearly flat at INR594 crores (vs INR591 crores).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The INR1,000 crore H2 requirement is a large step-up from H1, and it depends on monsoon ending and workforce recovery; the growth range was already trimmed once.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Alcon targets INR200 crores plus revenue in FY28 and Alcon can bid for contracts up to INR200 crores plus in its own name, but no new product launch was discussed.

rows.label: FY27 order inflow of minimum INR3,000 crores
rows.why: About INR1,490 crores secured so far, so at least INR2,000 crores is needed in H2, with no L1 positions currently disclosed.

rows.label: Africa ramp via Transnet contract
rows.why: FY27 Africa revenue expected about INR80 crores, and the 5-year INR385 crore Transnet contract should add about INR70-75 crores a year in South Africa.

rows.label: Working capital cycle reduction
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was INR54 crores vs INR12 crores in H1 FY26 (about 5x), though contract assets rose to about INR543 crores with about INR100 crores of retention.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 billing recovery, order inflows and the 14-15% margin, but cautious and vague on H1 execution and the timing of revenue acceleration; analysts pressed on how the INR1,000 crore H2 target would be reached.
